C++20 · Qt 6 · macOS · Linux

Nebula Code

An offline-first code editor built with Qt Widgets. Each window combines a folder explorer, tabbed Scintilla editors, and an optional interactive terminal.

Why I built it

I wanted a lightweight desktop editor with familiar development tools and a native C++ foundation.

Editing and workspace tools

  • Split views share documents and undo history, with independent cursor and scroll positions.
  • Quick Open, a command palette, find in files, simultaneous editing, syntax highlighting, and text wrapping.
  • An integrated terminal with configurable docking and persistent workspace sessions.
  • A local Git panel for diffs, staging, unstaging, and commits.
  • On-demand clangd integration for C/C++ completion, navigation, and diagnostics.

Platform support and tradeoffs

Nebula supports Intel and Apple Silicon Macs, plus x86-64 and ARM64 Linux. Git and clangd features use locally installed executables. Large files skip selected language and highlighting features to keep editing responsive.

Measured memory use

The repository reports median process-tree PSS of 35–70 MiB in seven-launch Ubuntu benchmark runs across two file sizes and x86-64 and ARM64. Those measurements use revision 6028b09, before text wrapping was added, and describe that test setup.
